answer: The declaration is a falcon header, so 4785 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in vault, as a result the distribution is public, and thread lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 26 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
